summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu and installs Google Chrome in it. It sets up a non-interactive environment to avoid prompts during installation, downloads Chrome, installs it, cleans up temporary files, and configures Chrome to run with specific performance flags when the container starts.

explanations.3: This environment variable tells the system to skip interactive prompts during package installation, which is necessary in Docker since there's no terminal to respond to questions.
explanations.5: The backslash at the end of this line and the next few lines chains multiple commands together into a single RUN instruction, which reduces the number of layers in the Docker image and keeps it smaller.
explanations.9: After installing Chrome, we delete the apt package cache to free up disk space in the image, since we won't need to install anything else.
explanations.11: CMD specifies what command runs automatically when the container starts—in this case, Chrome with two flags: one to avoid using shared memory (which can cause issues in Docker) and one to disable GPU acceleration (which isn't available in most containers).
